propositions: When acceptance criteria become stale or invalidated by subsequent code changes, the completion verifier blocks close and provides no legitimate sanctioned path forward except force-close or ref-pointing to old commits, both leaving inaccurate ticket state.

The correct remediation for stale criteria is to edit the ticket to match reality, re-pass plan review, and close against corrected criteria, but this workflow is undocumented and not obvious to users.

The --ref <commit> flag is a legitimate close path for criteria invalidated by later work (verified against the commit where work landed), but it is not documented as sanctioned in the close workflow.

The plan-review close gate's stale-regver check forces re-review of completed and merged work if the criteria registry changed since plan approval, stranding finished tickets and creating billable waste.
Criteria that are auto-generated or fundamentally unverifiable have no escape hatch at any commit ref and require an auditable disposition-classification system.
Automation-owned alert tickets (filed by bots) should have a closure path owned by the filing automation rather than blocked by code-verifiable completion criteria.
